Kifunensine further targets the Organic hydroperoxide resistance protein, putative, indicating a possible pathway through which ketoprofen may influence this protein. Similarly, ketoprofen is also associated with Myosin-14, which is a target of dihydrocodeine, which also targets the same protein. This suggests that ketoprofen may exert its effects through multiple intermediaries, ultimately influencing the Organic hydroperoxide resistance protein, putative. The evidence is consistent across two paths, with slight variations in confidence scores, but both support a functional link between ketoprofen and the target protein. The mechanism appears to involve the interaction of ketoprofen with Myosin-14, which then modulates the activity of the Organic hydroperoxide resistance protein, putative. The strength of the evidence is supported by multiple overlapping pathways, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
